title: Priv DNS + Egress Rulebook Terraform: SG / NACL / DNS / Egress Module
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Create a composable Terraform module that codifies Redwood's VPC security rulebook for private (VPC) deployments. The module must manage Security Groups (SGs), Network ACLs (NACLs), Private DNS forwarding/hosted zones, and egress policy primitives (allowlists, proxy routing hooks, and VPC endpoint helpers). This ticket covers API design for the module, migration strategy for existing stacks, upgrade/compatibility considerations, automated health checks, and CI validation.

Goals:
- Single, well-documented module consumers can instantiate to comply with Redwood security posture for private deployments.
- Safe defaults for new clusters but highly configurable for customer-specific exceptions.
- Clear upgrade path from previous ad-hoc IaC into the module with automated state import helpers.
- Runtime health checks and smoke tests to validate policies post-apply (DNS resolution, egress reachability, SG/NACL intended deny/allow checks).

Scope in this ticket:
- Terraform module source layout, inputs/outputs API, and naming conventions for resources and tags.
- Private DNS: support both Route53 private hosted zones and BIND-forwarder style zones via provided resolver IPs.
- SG rules: role-based SG templates (control-plane, runtime, management) with documented ephemeral port ranges and least-privilege defaults.
- NACLs: stateless layer with explicit ordering and migration plan for existing numbered entries. Provide example templates for allowlist wide-nets vs. service-specific rules.
- Egress: built-in support for (1) managed egress proxy endpoints, (2) VPC endpoints to cloud services, and (3) CIDR-based allowlists with an emergency open-mode toggle for troubleshooting.
- Upgrade tooling: terraform import helpers and a plan-validation script that detects conflicting SNAT/NAT Gateway configurations.
- Health checks: a terraform post-apply runner (shell + small Go binary) that executes DNS resolution checks for private zones, port connect tests through SGs, and simulated outgoing connections to validated egress targets.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- UI in Console for policy editing (will be tracked separately).
- Per-customer billing changes for dedicated egress gateways.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Module publishes a reproducible example that creates: one private hosted DNS zone, three SG roles (control, runtime, mgmt), NACL with ordered deny/allow rules, and an egress-policy resource that can select proxy vs nat.
2) Terraform plan for existing stacks runs with a migration helper that maps old security group names/tags to new module-managed SGs without destructive replacement in >=95% of cases.
3) Post-apply health-check runner returns green for DNS resolution of internal services, can open TCP handshake on allowed ports, and successfully egress to allowed endpoints; failures provide actionable diffs.
4) Module includes unit tests (terragrunt/inspec/terratest or equivalent) and CI job that validates plan-only and apply-in-a-non-prod workspace.
5) Security review completed and documented in Confluence with threat model and NACL ordering rationale.
implementation_notes:
Design decisions and trade-offs: prefer explicit SGs over broad SG generation to preserve least-privilege and easier audit. NACLs are used as a defense-in-depth layer for cross-account peering and shared subnets where SGs alone are insufficient. Private DNS supports two modes: managed-hosted-zone (Route53) or forwarder IPs (for on-prem hybrid) via module param resolver_mode.

Terraform specifics:
- Required providers: aws >= 5.0, external for post-apply hooks.
- Module inputs: environment (string), vpc_id, subnet_map (map of subnet ids by tier), resolver_mode ("hosted"|"forwarder"), forwarders (list of IPs), sg_definitions (list of objects encoded as json strings), nacl_definitions (list of json strings), egress_mode ("proxy"|"nat"|"endpoint"), emergency_open_tag (string).
- Outputs: sg_ids (map), nacl_ids (list), private_zone_id, egress_policy_id.

Migration path:
1) run terraform plan with migration_helper=true to get mapping suggestions.
2) apply in disabled-change mode (no replacements) to create module-managed resources that reference existing IDs.
3) flip ownership tag in a follow-up apply that marks resources as managed-by=terraform-module.

Health checks and monitoring:
- Add a CloudWatch/Datadog synthetic check that runs the post-apply runner on schedule.
- Expose metrics: dns_resolution_latency_ms, egress_connectivity_failures, nacl_denies_count.
